newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex gains in Q2, production at historic levels.
newsitem.headline: Pemex gains in Q2, production at historic levels.

text.p: Mexico's oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) managed a 6.7 percent increase in net profits amid higher production in the second quarter despite a collapse in international crude prices, Pemex chair Adrian Lajous said at a news conference on Tuesday.
The oil monopoly reported net profits before taxes of 41.96 billion pesos, and profits after rights and taxes of 5.297 billion pesos for the quarter.
Pemex produced a historic record of crude in June, breaking the three million barrels per day (bpd) level to arrive at an average 3.007 million bpd for the month.
But the record comes as Mexico's basket of crude oil hit an average of $15.13 per barrel in the second quarter, a fall of $2.13 from the year ago period.
Lower international crude prices took a bite into the monopoly's operating profits, Lajous added.
"The greater volume of production by Pemex Exploration and Production did not fully compensate for lower prices in the second quarter," he said.
The lower crude prices pushed operating profits down 4.7 percent in the period to 33.583 billion pesos versus the second quarter a year ago. Pemex's E&P was also hit by the drop in prices.

"The performance of Pemex Exploration and Production should be evaluated in the context of price reduction of $6 per barrel since the peak in December to June 1997 levels, the lowest prices in 20 months," Lajous said.

Pemex has embarked on an aggressive exploration plan for the coming years to further exploit Campeche Sound oil fields and natural gas in the Burgos Basin. Natural gas ouput rose by 100 million cubic feet per day (cfd) in the first half from the year-ago period, Pemex said.
The oil monopoly continued providing almost one of every three pesos of its sales to the federal government, Lajous said.

Pemex paid the federal government 77 billion pesos in taxes and rights in the first half of the year, or 20 percent more from the first six months of 1996. Taxes to the federal government took up 63 percent of sales and 91 percent of profits, the company said in a report.
The company's indirect tax burden more than doubled in the period, to cut Pemex's net profits after taxes and rights by 10.9 percent, the monopoly said.
